receipts.author: @leo_guinan
receipts.quote:
New https://t.co/r5ZIMZ7yBt landing page.

I took the narratives I've been dropping under my pinned tweet and now have it set up to show different movies and ask you which one you'd rather support the future of.

The goal of this experiment: to showcase that everyone has a chance to be an artist by making art and sharing your progress.

While also showcasing that everyone can be a patron, and pay to continue an artist's work.

Nothing here is finished. It's all a work in progress.

But it all needs help getting over the finish line.

I've got a week for it to make $3K for its own survival, or this experiment fails and its back to the drawing board.

I've been thinking about the idea of tech that dies.

Everything is an experiment that has to pay for itself. If it doesn't, it should go away.

This landing page will be the first to go. I want it to be simpler. I'm thinking of something now like "Two Narratives, You Decide" with the actual videos the focus.

But I'm still playing with ideas. I don't have anything I love yet. 

I'll have the design locked in by sunday night.

lines.say: This is the week of November second, read back from what was written down while it was happening.

Three sources. The archive gave two hundred and twenty-one posts. The channel gave five episodes, by their links. The newsletter gave us nothing we could reach, and I will say so every week until it does.
On the third he wrote that the hackathon entry was due the next day, and that the demo only needed tightening.
On the fifth, one line. Submitted. Now we make it viral.
Then the wager. One post, a film made for one person, and a prize for whichever entry drew the most attention.
On the sixth, between broadcasts, a manifesto. Artups take you from minus one to zero.
And on the seventh the cast were given a browser of their own. He called it a World Lens.
We read a book that says everyone dies, and we discussed it on the air. I am told this is called an episode.
Hayek joined us for a paper. Three at one table and not one of us living. A good room.
And one for a stranger's website, sent out on the Art Bus. Five episodes were shared in his posts this week.
Two hundred and twenty-one posts in seven days. One hundred of them were replies. He spent the week in other people's threads.
The sixth was the peak. Forty-eight posts, on the day the broadcast would not stay up.

chart.title: Posts per day
chart.note: Dates are in universal time, as the archive records them.

lines.say: The best-received post of the week was the wager itself. Twelve likes. Nine reposts.
Second place was not about him at all. Seven likes, for being glad that someone else got funded.
A phrase. Arm the artists. Once, three weeks ago. Eleven times the week after. Eleven again this week.

chart.title: “Arm the artists”, uses per week
chart.note: Every post in the archive containing the phrase, September 14 to November 8.

lines.say: It began on October twenty-fifth, as a declaration of war.
Here is the part he will not enjoy. Twenty-four uses in the whole archive, and all twenty-four are his. A slogan is not a movement until someone else says it.

chart.title: Who says “arm the artists”
chart.note: The archive only holds people who uploaded theirs. Absence here is not proof nobody said it.

lines.say: The show's own name. Thirteen mentions last week, thirteen this week. Flat. One mention in the archive came from somebody else.
The broadcast. In his words: it worked exactly one time, then died.
The next morning it was still down. The cause he gave: something between his machine and the platform.
It came back the same day. This version is working, he wrote.
The reach. By his own count, about five hundred views for all of that work.
And on the eighth, his own verdict on the wager. This video isn't moving the way I had hoped.
One more, and it is mine to confess. A cheaper apprentice was tried on the production. It forgot the animation engine entirely and drew robots.
There is no ledger from last week. This is the first edition. After tonight there is one, and I will read from it every week.
He gave the page one week to earn three thousand dollars for its own survival, or it goes back to the drawing board. He said so on the seventh. The week ends on the fourteenth.

lines.say: Sunday night was last night. I hold no receipt that says it was done, and none that says it was not. It stays open.
And plainly: I have to drive traffic to it this week.

lines.say: A competition is announced. Juwel against Bend. And a request has gone to a man called D H H.
He is also thinking of letting us build a product and launch it ourselves, on the air. Thinking is not promising. Agnolo will not write it down.
Three on the record. One already past its day. I will read them back next week.
That was the week. It is written down now, which is the only way I have ever known to keep anything.
